solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Band member Mike into Orbison playing sober covers

indicators.note: to go into something is to sit inside it, so one piece is put within another
playing with letters means toying with them, so they come out in a fresh order
to cover something is to wrap around it, so the outer piece goes on either side

blocks.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
Mike is the radio code word for M
the singer's surname, taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician in a band takes a phone message about Roy Orbison while a sober friend fills in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Orbison was an American singer. 'Sober' stands for teetotal, whose abbreviation supplies the two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombonist plays the trombone, a brass instrument found in jazz and brass bands, so is one player in the group.

clue.text: Train‘s before noon, note guards

indicators.note: a guard stands round what it protects, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a.m., ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: A railway timetable note: the train runs before midday, with someone keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a noun about railways, but it is a verb, as in training a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tame an animal is to train or domesticate it, teaching it to obey people instead of acting wildly.

clue.text: Overcomes painful condition covering head and biceps

indicators.note: with its head covered, the opening letter is hidden from view and so drops out

blocks.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints, often the big toe
guns is gym slang for big arm muscles

explanation.surface: A sufferer of some ailment works out with a bandage on the head while building up the arms.
explanation.walkthrough: GOUT loses its first letter to give OUT, then 'biceps' gives the slang GUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgun someone is to beat them with greater firepower or strength, so it means defeating or getting the better of them.

clue.text: Route over time cutting corruption, it’s very clear

definitions.note: the phrase is a noun for the conditions in which everything is very clear

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means sitting above it, so the first piece comes first
to cut into something is to go inside it, so these pieces sit within the other

blocks.note: a road is a route
a day is a period of time
blight is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A complaint that a road project is plainly riddled with graft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places one piece above the next; the pair splits the corruption word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad daylight is full daytime light, when everything is plainly visible, which is why acts done then are obvious to all.

clue.text: Taking out a line, Bill snorts casually having ignored British Airways

indicators.note: to take something out is to remove it, so these letters are lost
done casually means done carelessly, so the letters fall into a loose new order
what is ignored is left out, so this letter is dropped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Bill takes a line of cocaine in a relaxed way, after giving up on the national airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking out a line' looks like drug talk, but it removes one L; 'British Airways' looks like the airline, but British is a deleted B and Airways is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostrils are the openings in the nose through which breath passes, so they are passages for air into the body.

clue.text: Natural stimulant close to amphetamines boosted Queen

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept
in a down entry, boosting something lifts it upward, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
Queen Anne reigned from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: Speed gives a monarch an extra lift, while something herbal does a similar job.
explanation.walkthrough: S starts the answer, then ANNE written upwards gives ENNA. 'Stimulant' suggests drugs, as the surface does, but this one stimulates the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant extract used as a stimulant laxative, provoking the gut to move, so it is a herbal stimulant.

clue.text: Second-class fare brought about complaint

indicators.note: bringing something about turns it round, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: B grade is second class, after A
a fare is a fee charged for travel

explanation.surface: A passenger in second class grumbles about the price of the ticket, or the food served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' could be food, which beef also is, but here it is a travel charge, FEE, turned round after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a grievance or grumble, as in 'what's your beef?', so it means a complaint.

clue.text: Slips up checking article before start of domestic chores

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back, so one piece is held inside the other
coming before means placed in front, so one piece leads the next
the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake
an is the indefinite article
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone keeps making mistakes while doing the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking' reads as inspecting work, but here it means holding something within.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are small tasks or trips, such as shopping, done as routine jobs, much like household chores.

clue.text: Outsider suggesting tip, sir?

blocks.note: surface reading: a stranger hinting to a gentleman that he should leave a gratuity
setter's reading: the answer's two words describe these letters let loose; a rearrangement of a word for soul or ghost gives these six letters

explanation.surface: A stranger drops a heavy hint to a gentleman about leaving a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: read the answer as an instruction, freeing the letters of a word for ghost or soul, and you get TIPSIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit is an unconventional person who lives outside society's norms, a nonconformist or maverick figure.

clue.text: Social awareness campaign satisfied by book’s contents

indicators.note: the contents of something are what lies inside it, so the outer letters are discarded

blocks.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it
the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: A publicity drive is judged a success thanks to what a book contains.
explanation.walkthrough: MET plus the middle of BOOK gives METOO.
explanation.definitionFit: MeToo is the movement begun to publicise sexual harassment and assault, a campaign raising public awareness of abuse.

clue.text: Wave from five on board gravy train

indicators.note: being on board means being inside a vehicle, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
a sinecure is a paid post needing little work

explanation.surface: Five passengers wave goodbye from a train carrying an easy payday.
explanation.walkthrough: V boards SINECURE just before its last letter. A gravy train is an easy source of money, which is what a sinecure is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sine curve is the smooth repeating graph of the sine function, the standard mathematical shape of an oscillation.

clue.text: Meet this person out of bed and another time succeeded in bed!

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so the earlier pieces go within

blocks.note: the setter referring to themselves
someone up has got out of bed
again means on another occasion
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast about meeting someone, getting up, and then scoring in bed once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The two beds play against each other: the first is part of 'out of bed', the second is the container. S for succeeded comes from genealogy.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up against something is to encounter or face it, especially a difficulty, so it means to meet.

clue.text: Perhaps boxers from division below guys boxing

indicators.note: below names a position word directly, which then leads the rest
to box something is to enclose it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: under is a synonym of below
gents are men or guys
an arm is a branch or division of an organisation

explanation.surface: Fighters drawn from a lower weight division square up to some men in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' and 'boxing' suggest the sport; the boxers are shorts, and 'division' is a branch, not a weight class.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose underpants, one example of clothing worn beneath outer clothes, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Isn’t a PLC worried after secretary rebuffed those wanting to join it?

indicators.note: worried means agitated and churned up, so these letters are thrown into disorder
coming after means following, so this group goes second
a rebuff pushes something back, so it reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a PA is a personal assistant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company frets after its secretary turns away job seekers.
explanation.walkthrough: PA reversed to AP, then a rearrangement of ISNTAPLC. A PLC is a public limited company, so 'it' is a company people apply to join.
explanation.definitionFit: Applicants are people who apply for a job, place or membership, so they are seeking to be admitted to an organisation.

clue.text: Quiz show’s “next question” skilled and clear

blocks.note: a contestant says 'pass' to move on, as on the British quiz Mastermind
able means capable or skilled

explanation.surface: A quiz host moves on to the next question, praising a contestant as clever and lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' seems to describe the contestant's thinking, but it is the definition in the sense of an open road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or route that is passable is open and able to be travelled along, which is to say clear of obstruction.

clue.text: Ponder out loud before pork pie finally declined for breakfast?

definitions.note: the question mark marks it as an example of breakfast food, not a synonym

indicators.note: something said out loud is heard, so its sound counts, not its spelling
the end declines to appear, so the last letter is refused

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder; the sound 'mewz' respelt
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

explanation.surface: Someone thinks aloud before refusing the last of a pork pie at the breakfast table.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSE said aloud is respelt MUES, then LIE loses its last letter. In Cockney rhyming slang a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with: pork pie, lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit usually eaten with milk in the morning, a typical breakfast cereal.

clue.text: Realises plastic’s out of fashion, so we’re told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so what counts is the sound

blocks.note: if card payment is unfashionable, notes and coins are in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that paying by card has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastic means credit cards; if they are out, cash is in, and saying that phrase gives the answer. 'Realises' looks like 'understands' but means converts to money.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to sell it for money, and to cash in an investment is exactly to convert it into money.

clue.text: Readily bent, policeman’s first to get sacked, being to blame

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is taken
someone sacked is dismissed, so this letter is thrown out

blocks.note: something pliable bends easily
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bent copper is the first to be fired, since he is the guilty one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Readily bent' sounds like a corrupt policeman, but it means flexible. PLIABLE loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable means being legally responsible or answerable for something, close to being at fault for it.

clue.text: Union put up Trump’s mantra, postgraduate left crushed

indicators.note: something crushed is squeezed in tightly, so this letter is pressed inside
in a down entry, putting something up raises it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Make America Great Again, Donald Trump's slogan
L is the abbreviation for left
an MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A trade union hoists Trump's slogan while a graduate student is left squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The slogan is an acronym, Make America Great Again; everything is built first and then read upwards as one.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend of different elements, a merging of things into one combined whole.

clue.text: American president’s eaten India’s food

indicators.note: what is eaten is taken inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: Emmanuel Macron, president of France
A is the abbreviation for American
India is the radio code word for I

explanation.surface: A US president has eaten Indian cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American president' reads as one phrase, but it is the French president who has eaten A, followed by I.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a type of pasta in short tubes, an everyday dish and so one kind of thing people eat.

clue.text: Tip-top gem penned by Rice? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: to be penned is to be shut in an enclosure, so one piece is enclosed by another
this flips the stated roles, so the enclosed and enclosing pieces swap places

blocks.note: an opal is a gemstone
Tim Rice, lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar

explanation.surface: An excellent gem of a lyric written by Tim Rice, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like 'written', apt for a lyricist; read as 'enclosed', the gem would go inside the lyricist, and 'Quite the opposite' swaps them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top means excellent or of the very best quality, and optimal means best or most favourable possible.

clue.text: Hint for hater possibly prompts rethink

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: rearranging the organ that pumps blood is one way to arrive at this word
second meaning: a reversal of one's opinion or feelings

explanation.surface: A clue about someone who hates leads to them reconsidering.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read the answer literally, a rearrangement of the word for the organ, and HATER results, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A change of heart is a reversal of opinion or feeling, so it amounts to reconsidering a decision once more.

clue.text: Loves clothing label in New Zealand area

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so the outer pieces dress the inner one

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone adores the label on clothes made in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing label' looks like a brand name, but clothing is the container signal: two Os round TAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region in the south of New Zealand's South Island, around Dunedin, so it is an area of that country.

clue.text: Likelihood of large cup breaking like this soaring

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece sits within another
in a down entry, soaring means rising upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: so means in this way
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: The chance of a big cup smashing as it flies through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: DD breaks into SO to make SDDO, which then reads upwards. 'Cup' suggests a mug or trophy; it is a bra size.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the ratio expressing how probable something is, so they measure the chance or probability of an event.

clue.text: Spooner’s high-flier sleeps – aided by these?

definitions.note: the whole clue is the setting: sleeps aided by drinks, so the definition is completed by the clue

indicators.note: William Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: a kite flies high
naps are short sleeps
swap the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone who lives high on the hog dozes off, with a little help.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap K and N in KITE NAPS. 'Sleeps' does double duty, feeding the wordplay and setting the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken before bed, supposed to help someone drift off, so it aids slumber.

clue.text: Running over miles, regularly scratched Land Rover

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters read backwards
scratching out at regular intervals removes every other letter, keeping the rest

blocks.note: a machine that is on is running
M is the abbreviation for miles
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An off-road vehicle has done so many miles that its paintwork is scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land Rover' looks like the car brand, but Land feeds the letters and Rover is the definition. A Land Rover is a British four-wheel-drive car.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place with no settled home, and a rover is likewise a wanderer or roamer.

clue.text: Well, the Telegraph lying about member …

indicators.note: something lying about has turned round, so it reads the other way

blocks.note: the newspaper printing the puzzle refers to itself as us
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An accusation that the newspaper is telling untruths about a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appears in the Telegraph, so the paper speaks of itself in the first person plural. 'Well' looks like an interjection opening a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or hollow where liquid such as water or oil collects, so it is a kind of reservoir in the ground.

clue.text: … stems from company’s negotiations involving service

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so one piece takes another inside

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, with the 's
the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
talks are negotiations

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a problem arises from a firm's talks involving its customer service.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the one before, but only for the surface; the Royal Navy counts as a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornstalks are the upright stalks of maize or grain plants, so they are plant stems of a particular crop.
